investigations.name: aim1-vaginal-bv
investigations.title: Aim 1 — Hormone-Regulated Vaginal Microbiome (BV)
investigations.description:
BV affects more than 20 million women in the US and arises from dysbiosis of the vaginal microbiome, where the interaction between microbial dynamics and the host environment makes the condition hard to resolve. Two women receiving the same BV treatment can show very different recurrence because of interactions among vaginal microbial ecology, estrogen-regulated epithelial physiology, immune responses, and antibiotic exposure.

This investigation builds Aim 1 of MOSAIC: a multi-scale, hormone-regulated model of the vaginal microbiome. Mechanistic community models (Arnold lab) capture macro-level population dynamics; genome-scale metabolic models (Reconstructor-built, transcriptome-informed) resolve intracellular metabolism of key species in a simulated vaginal niche; and a PKPD compartment supplies the estrogen state. The in vitro reproductive-tract Transwell platform (Derre lab) is the testbed for parameterization and validation. Demonstration therapeutics: metronidazole and L. crispatus.

investigations.name: aim2-gut-liver-masld
investigations.title: Aim 2 — Gut–Liver Host–Microbiome Metabolism (MASLD)
investigations.description:
MASLD affects nearly 100 million people in the US; nearly half of affected individuals are women, with marked differences between pre- and post-menopausal populations. It emerges from a complex interplay between liver metabolism, gut microbial ecology, immune response, and hormone regulation, with perturbations in one subsystem propagating across scales.

This investigation builds Aim 2 of MOSAIC: a multi-compartment framework coupling genome-scale representations of male and female hepatic metabolism (Human1-derived, ftINIT-contextualized) with community metabolic models of the gut microbiome (Klebsiella, Escherichia, Streptococcus, Faecalibacterium, Roseburia). The Khetani-lab 3D liver microtissues and the gut–liver Transwell model are the in vitro testbeds. Demonstration therapeutics: resmetirom (a thyroid hormone receptor-beta agonist) and GLP-1 receptor agonists (e.g. semaglutide), both with documented sex-dependent responses.

investigations.name: aim3-integration
investigations.title: Aim 3 — Compartment-Coupled Integration
investigations.description:
Aim 3 is the integration layer and the core software deliverable of MOSAIC. It connects the vaginal and gut–liver models from Aims 1 and 2 to explicitly simulate the synthesis, microbial deconjugation, enterohepatic recycling, and systemic transport of sex hormones across biological compartments. The central design principle is that each component model keeps its own assumptions, units, and biological scope; MOSAIC supplies executable interfaces (built on Vivarium / process-bigraph) that let one model's outputs serve as another's inputs or constraints — metabolite exchange, hormone production and recycling, growth rates, community composition, and agent behavior.

This investigation hosts the seam itself: the shared hormone store, the typed interfaces between GEM / community / PKPD / agent-based Processes, and the system-level studies that test whether perturbations propagate correctly across compartments.
